mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings and consumer demand, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0 and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods where UNRATE > 6% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for three consecutive months signals persistent inflation, prompting anticipation of tighter monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
